requirements_excerpt.requirement: Provide a first-class accessible List view driven by the same normalized relationship data as Map, with equivalent substantive information and navigation.
acceptance: AT-16: Map/List switching retains selection, filters, returned scope, relationship IDs, direction, and warnings. List users can open entries, inspect evidence, focus a term, and request more connections with the same semantics.

AT-29: Major reading and exploration tasks can be completed through keyboard and list without canvas, dragging, hover, or double-click. A small control set avoids hundreds of invisible graph controls in tab order; meaningful result/selection changes are announced rather than every layout frame.

requirements_excerpt.requirement: Target WCAG 2.2 AA using semantic navigation, headings, inputs, buttons, lists, visible unobscured focus, and keyboard alternatives for every essential action.
acceptance: Search retains a visible labeled input and submit action; autocomplete follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with Arrow Up/Down, Enter, and Escape that dismisses suggestions without erasing the query. Command/Ctrl+K may supplement but never replace visible search.

The page does not use a whole-page application role merely for the graph. Zoom, Fit current view, Focus here, source inspection, and other essential actions work without dragging, hovering, double-clicking, or memorized shortcuts.

Normal text meets 4.5:1 contrast and large text/relevant non-text controls meet their applicable requirements; the WCAG 2.2 AA 24-by-24 CSS-pixel target criterion and its exceptions are assessed correctly. Color is supplemented by labels/icons/line styles, with selection more prominent than decoration.

requirements_excerpt.requirement: Manage focus and announcements across sources, menus, navigation, and asynchronous reads without trapping users or discarding context.
acceptance: Opening a source drawer moves focus to its heading or first meaningful control; closing it restores the evidence trigger. Escape closes temporary menus/drawers and returns focus predictably; route changes do not leave focus in removed components.
Loading preserves current context, errors stay beside the failed region, and updates announce meaningful changes rather than continuous layout frames or whole-page blank flashes.

requirements_excerpt.requirement: Keep the reader and surrounding controls operable and legible across narrow layouts, substantial zoom, both themes, and reduced-motion settings.
acceptance: AT-30: At a 320 CSS-pixel viewport and with substantial browser zoom, menus and text reflow, controls remain usable, and status remains legible. Spatial-diagram exceptions do not excuse non-reflowing surrounding UI.

Narrow navigation becomes a drawer and entry text receives primary space; a phone Map is dedicated with dismissible selected details and a visible List option. Process/source text reads vertically without squeezed parallel columns.

Light and dark themes receive independent checks; reduced motion stops unnecessary animation and settled layouts. System fonts, comfortable line spacing, restrained surfaces, and small consistent spacing support reading; exact visual tuning remains proposed in Decisions.

requirements_excerpt.requirement: Supply a requirement-to-implementation-and-evidence matrix covering all SRC AT-01 through AT-36 with real canonical fixtures and the actual production bundle.
acceptance: Unit evidence covers normalization/ranking/category mappings/cursors, relation identities/direction, graph-list projection, source selection, and state transitions; service evidence covers isolation, assets, sessions, freshness, budgets, snapshot conflict, non-mutation, and inaccessible writes.

Browser evidence covers search-entry-history, selection/focus, sources, keyboard, responsiveness, expiry, CSP, renderer failure, and production offline operation; manual evidence covers readability, focus, screen-reader use, relationship comprehension, and knowledge tasks. Tool choice may use Playwright or the established equivalent.

A production build, explicit launch, safe reads, search/process access, interactive map/text equivalence, root/Template behavior, updated docs, and preserved agent workflows each have direct evidence. Skips, pre-existing failures, content gaps, environment limits, and untested behavior remain separate from passes; screenshots or unit tests alone never establish integrated completion.

requirements_excerpt.requirement: Evaluate the actual interface against its WCAG 2.2 AA target with automated browser checks and manual keyboard/screen-reader use, reporting tested environments precisely.
acceptance: Evidence names actual browser and assistive-technology versions/combinations, including the relevant macOS VoiceOver/Safari walkthrough; a Windows screen-reader/browser combination is added when available, otherwise that limit is reported.
Automated scan results supplement manual knowledge-task and focus checks; component-library selection or a passing scanner never supports an unqualified accessibility/compliance claim.
